他依然自信如初，似乎沒有被最近的問題所困擾。
The factory closure is seemingly inevitable.
看來，工廠關閉勢在難免。
Seemingly, she's gone to live with another man.
看樣子，她去和另外一個男人同居了。

NONE: › socially suitable and polite
合適的；得體的

example: Opposite
unseemly

NONE: › past participle of see
（see的過去分詞）
› to move or spread slowly out of a hole or through something
滲出；滲漏

example: Pesticides are seeping out of farmland and into the water supply.
殺蟲劑正從農田中滲出，進入供水系統。
figurative Given the intense secrecy of the arms business, information only seeps out in company literature.
由於軍火貿易極度保密，只能從公司的資料中獲得一點蛛絲馬跡。

NONE: › a person who says he or she can see what will happen in the future
預言家；先知
› a light cloth that has a pattern of raised and flat strips on it
泡泡紗；縐條紋薄織物
› a long board that children play on. The board is balanced on a central point so that when a child sits on each end they can make the board go up and down by pushing off the ground with their feet.
蹺蹺板
› to change repeatedly from one emotion, situation, etc. to another and then back again
（情緒、局勢等）搖擺不定，不斷反覆，交替

example: His mind seesawed between hope and despair all through those weeks.
那幾個星期裡，他一會兒心懷希望，一會兒又感到絕望，心情陰晴不定。

I: › to feel very angry but to be unable or unwilling to express it clearly
› (of a large number or amount) to move around energetically in a small space
（大量人或物在狹小的空間內）密集，雲集；充滿

example: The rest of the class positively seethed with indignation when Julia won the award.
茱莉亞得獎的時候，全班明顯很不服氣。
By the end of the meeting he was seething.
會議結束時他氣呼呼的。
The streets were seething (= busy and crowded) with tourists.
街道上遊客摩肩接踵。
